events.factual_description: Bunkamura presents Shun Ishiwaka Trio in Meet The Artists vol.9 at Cecion Suginami Hall on Sunday, November 1, 2026. Doors are at 14:30 and the performance starts at 15:00. The announced trio is Shun Ishiwaka on drums, Marty Holoubek on bass, and Yusei Takahashi on piano. Bunkamura lists general reserved admission at ¥4,500 and describes the 491-seat hall program as a performance in which rhythm itself becomes the protagonist, built from Ishiwaka's movement between jazz, improvisation, contemporary music and pop. Ishiwaka's official site says this core trio was formed in 2024; its first album, Live at ALFIE “Temporal Cubic,” was released in December 2025 and nominated for the Music Awards Japan 2026 jazz-album category. The same artist source documents the trio's September 2, 2026 release mabui as a trio-plus-one project with saxophonist Tomoaki Baba; Baba is not announced for this Cecion Suginami performance and is not included in the event lineup.

en.why_it_matters: Ishiwaka puts rhythm at the center without turning the trio into a drum showcase: Holoubek and Takahashi give him a compact acoustic frame where pulse, structure and improvisation can keep changing roles. There is also a quiet Listening Notes resonance in hearing the core trio whose first album was recorded live at ALFIE, now presented in a hall program explicitly built around Ishiwaka's rhythmic language.
en.trip_verdict: If November 1 is already a Tokyo day, this is a strong afternoon option in Suginami and worth catching when the schedule lines up. I would not reorganize a Kanto itinerary around this date alone because the trio is active and no one-off context is announced.

es.why_it_matters: Ishiwaka pone el ritmo en el centro sin convertir al trío en una exhibición de batería: Holoubek y Takahashi le dan un marco acústico compacto donde pulso, estructura e improvisación pueden cambiar de función todo el tiempo. Además hay una resonancia discreta con Listening Notes: es el núcleo del trío cuyo primer disco se grabó en vivo en ALFIE, ahora llevado a una sala que presenta esta función precisamente alrededor del lenguaje rítmico de Ishiwaka.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 1 de noviembre ya es un día de Tokio, sí aprovecharía la tarde en Suginami cuando embone con el resto del plan. No reorganizaría un itinerario por Kanto alrededor de esta fecha sola porque el trío está activo y no hay un contexto único anunciado.
